newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil high court to rule on CVRD case.
newsitem.headline: Brazil high court to rule on CVRD case.

text.p: Brazil's highest court, the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), was due to consider later Monday the latest request for an injunction to halt the privatization of mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).

A full session of the STF was due to meet at 1400 local time/1700 GMT to study a constitutional challenge to the sell-off brought by the Order of Brazilian Lawyers (OAB), a guild representing Brazil's legal profession, an STF spokesman said.

The case is one of dozens lodged with courts across Brazil against the privatization of CVRD. The government hopes to begin the sale April 29 with the auction of 45 percent of the firm's voting shares on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange.

First, however, the government must reverse an injunction issued Friday by a judge in Sao Paulo. Lawyers representing the National Development Bank (BNDES) were expected to appeal that injunction later Monday.

The OAB case due to be heard in the STF today argues the privatization of CVRD breaks constitutional rules which state that private companies can only provide public services after winning a public tender to do so, an OAB lawyer said.
As well as its mining activities, CVRD operates rail and port services which would automatically be transferred to its new private owners after privatization.
The STF last week threw out another OAB constitutional challenge to the CVRD sell-off.
